title: Count flops against bytes, then build a key-value cache
brief: Compute the flops per byte of a weight matrix, the time one token takes to read the weights, and the batch that saturates a chip, then size a KV cache, build one, and decode through it with the same answer as a full recompute.
hints: A matrix times a batch of B vectors does 2 * B flops per weight and reads b bytes per weight, so the ratio is 2 * B / b. Decoding one token reads every weight once, so the time is n_params * bytes_per_elt / bandwidth.
The ridge point is peak_flops / bandwidth. You need 2 * B / b >= ridge, so B >= ridge * b / 2. Round up, because a batch is a whole number.
kv_cache_bytes is 2 * n_layer * n_kv * d_head * seq_len * bytes_per_elt. The leading 2 is one copy for keys and one for values.
KVCache.append should add one array of shape (n_kv, d_head) to a per-layer list. KVCache.get should np.stack that list on axis 0, and return empty (0, n_kv, d_head) arrays when nothing is stored.
cached_attention_step: scores = K @ q / sqrt(d_head), softmax them (subtract the max first), then return weights @ V. One query against T cached rows gives a (d_head,) vector.
